problem: Make a daily news briefing for the team.

lenses.title: Problem first
lenses.question: Is this the right problem — and whose is it?
lenses.without: Build a feed that pulls every headline every morning.
lenses.with: Asked the team what they actually did with news. Real problem: nobody had time to judge what was relevant to their work.

lenses.title: User before feature
lenses.question: What job is the reader really trying to do?
lenses.with: Readers skim on the way to standup. They need a 2-minute read that tells them if anything needs action today.

lenses.title: First principles
lenses.question: What actually needs to be true?
lenses.without: Copy the format of existing newsletters.
lenses.with: Started from three questions: What happened? Why does it matter? Who is affected? These shaped the filtering and summary structure.

lenses.title: Systems thinking
lenses.question: Where does the process break?
lenses.without: Fix bad summaries one by one.
lenses.with: Mapped the pipeline: source → filter → summarize → deliver. Most errors came from the filter step, so I fixed it there once.
lenses.trailStep: Fixed errors at the filter step

lenses.title: Trade-offs and outcomes
lenses.question: What do I cut, and how will I know it worked?
lenses.without: Ship every feature at once and count clicks.
lenses.with: Cut personalization from v1. Measured one thing: did readers act on at least one item per week?
lenses.trailStep: v1 scoped, measured by actions taken

result: A briefing the team actually reads — and acts on.
